blocks.h2: What Does an Ejector Pump Do?
blocks.body: Basement fixtures that sit below the sewer line can't drain on their own. They empty into a sealed basin, and the ejector pump pushes the wastewater up and out to the main line. A float starts the pump, and a check valve stops the water from falling back. In homes with an overhead sewer, the same kind of pump handles every basement drain.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber working on the discharge pipe of a basement sump pump

blocks.h2: Signs Your Ejector Pump Needs Help

tiles.body: Water in the basin is too high.
Often the lid seal or the vent.
A stuck float or bad check valve.

blocks.intro: Many Skokie basements have an ejector pump, either for a basement bathroom or as part of an overhead sewer.

items.body: If your basement was converted to an overhead sewer, the ejector pump is what keeps it working. When it fails, every basement drain stops.
Washers draining to the basin send lint that wears out pumps. A lint trap helps.
Pumps installed 15 or 20 years ago are due for replacement.
We test the alarm on every visit. See [overhead sewer systems](/skokie/overhead-sewer-systems).

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: We fix the pump and explain what failed.

steps.body: Pump, float, check valve, lid and vent.

blocks.h2: Ejector Pumps in Overhead Sewer Systems
blocks.body: Many Skokie homes with overhead sewers rely on an ejector pump to lift every drop of basement wastewater. If that pump fails, the basement fixtures back up, even in dry weather. We replace failed pumps with units sized for the system, check the float and check valve and test the alarm. A second pump or battery backup adds protection if you use the basement every day.

blocks.h2: Ejector Pump Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: My overhead sewer pump stopped. What do I do?
items.preview: Stop using basement drains and call us.
items.answer: Stop using the laundry, floor drain and any basement fixtures, and call us. Without the pump, the basin will overflow.

items.q: How long do ejector pumps last?
items.answer: Often around 7 to 10 years, depending on use.

items.q: Why does the basement smell like sewer?
items.preview: A worn seal, vent issue or dry trap.
items.answer: Usually a worn basin lid seal, a vent connection or a floor drain trap that dried out.

items.q: Can you add a second pump as a backup?
items.answer: Sometimes. Some basins can hold a duplex setup with two pumps. We'll look at yours.

items.q: How do I know if my overhead sewer pump is working?
items.answer: Run water in a basement fixture and listen for the pump to start and stop.

items.q: How much does ejector pump replacement cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on the pump and basin. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, the basin and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
